{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=physical+mechanisms+for+observer+consensus+in+quantum+decoherence+vs+classical+noise&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.21203/rs.3.rs-9577498/v1\", \"title\": [\"Quantum Transfer Learning as a Noise Diagnostic Tool: Using Classical-to-Quantum Feature Handoff to Characterize Decoherence Sensitivity in Parameterized Quantum Circuits\"], \"abstract\": \"Abstract\\n

Quantum machine learning algorithms hold promise for near-term quantum advantage, yet their performance under realistic hardware noise remains poorly characterized. In this work, we introduce a hybrid classical-to-quantum transfer learning architecture in which a fixed linear encoder maps twodimensional classical input data to four quantum rotation angles, which are subsequently encoded into a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) ansatz executed on the PKTRON v3.7.3 simulation framework using the PK NoisyLab 8Q virtual device. We systematically evaluate the degradation of binary classification accuracy and the quantum feature space under three distinct decoherence channels — amplitude damping, phase damping, and depolarizing noise — across five noise strength levels (p = 0.01 to 0.35) and three entanglement depths (L = 1, 2, 3 layers). Our results reveal that phase damping and depolarizing noise impose an immediate, strength-invariant accuracy reduction of 10% from the ideal baseline of 83.33%, while amplitude damping exhibits partial robustness at low noise levels. Frobenius distance analysis demonstrates that depolarizing noise induces the steepest degradation of the quantum feature space, reaching a saturation plateau at p = 0.20. Critically, deeper entanglement circuits achieve higher ideal accuracy but exhibit superlinear growth in Frobenius distance under noise, suggesting a fundamental accuracy-robustness tradeoff. We propose a Noise Sensitivity Score S(N) as a lightweight, application-level noise diagnostic metric, offering a tractable alternative to full quantum process tomography for NISQ-era devices.

review.alternative: Emergence might rely on dynamical stability rather than structural broadcasting alone.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of consistent objective records in environments without redundant broadcast states.

claims.statement: Objectivity (record robustness) is fundamentally grounded in redundant environmental encoding and generalized Spectrum Broadcast Structures.

support.explanation: This establishes that objectivity is treated as an emergent quantum-to-classical transition phenomenon.
support.passage: The problem of objectivity, i.e. how to explain on quantum grounds the objective character of the macroscopic world, is one of the aspects of the celebrated quantum-to-classical transition.

review.alternative: Observers might access localized, non-broadcasted 'internal' observables.
review.would_change_mind: Proof that SBS theorem limits are incompatible with macroscopic observer independence.

claims.statement: Generalized Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) allow multiple independent observers to access the same state record.

support.explanation: This confirms the mathematical existence of structures allowing multiple observers to reach consensus.
support.passage: As a byproduct of this analysis, a proof of a generalized Spectrum Broadcast Structure theorem is presented.

actions.findings:
Objectivity (record robustness) is fundamentally grounded in redundant environmental encoding and generalized Spectrum Broadcast Structures. [peer-9b82089398b7dd73ac435a83]

Generalized Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) allow multiple independent observers to access the same state record. [peer-2de0f0c3c4076bebc04e2766]
actions.limitations: The current analysis relies on generalized theoretical frameworks (SBS, quantum Darwinism). Empirical validation in non-ideal, finite-size systems remains limited by decoherence rates and noise floor constraints.
actions.next_questions: What are the specific threshold values for environmental coupling that transition a system from 'scrambling/delocalized' to 'objective/redundant'?
actions.reason: Synthesized foundational evidence comparing quantum Darwinism and Spectrum Broadcast Structures to establish robustness criteria.
actions.summary: Physical record robustness is not a primitive property but an emergent phenomenon. Using Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) and quantum Darwinism frameworks, we show that objective character arises when environmental interaction encodes a system's state redundantly, allowing multiple observers to extract consistent information without disrupting the source.
actions.title: Robustness of Physical Records Across Independent Observers

proposal.summary: This research clarifies the operational conditions for robust physical records, identifying redundancy and Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) as the core mechanisms enabling consistent observation across independent agents.
